newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 25.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The U.S. Justice Department gave approval to Bell Atlantic for its $23 billion acquisition of NYNEX Corp.
* Large accounting firms are moving to rid themselves of public companies if they worry those companies' financial practices could lead to future lawsuits.
* American Express net income rose 15 percent in the quarter compared to a year ago, boosted by strength in its credit card operations.
* After taking a more wary approach to investing in Asia, Chrysler is planning a major step into the region.
* The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 20.47 at 6792.25 points.
* While McDonald's launches its 55-cent Big Mac promotion, many McDonald restaurants have raised the prices of drinks and fries.
* A U.S. tobacco settlement could spark litigation overseas, where cigarette makers are looking to grow.

* Court records show a federal bankruptcy judge in Boston ruled that Sears's method of collecting debt from credit-card holders in bankruptcy proceedings was illegal in November 1995 and in February 1996.
* Analysts said the G-7 meeting this weekend in Washington would yield more talk against the higher dollar.
* Short interest on the Nasdaq Stock Market rose 6.3 percent to a record 1.53 billion shares in the latest month.
* Bankers Trust New York intends to buy NationsBank's institutional trust business.
* Kaiser Permanente and the AFL-CIO reached a pact which is expected to give Kaiser employees more input into patient care and bring the HMO more union workers as customers.
* Airlines Delta and Southwest reported better-than-expected profits, keeping with the industry's trend this quarter.
* A real-estate tax case in Boston could be the forerunner of cases under which office-tower owners could claim assessments were too high in the early 1990s.

* Heard on the Street: If a chief executive names his friends to his company's board, some might say that raises ethical issues. A new study by three professors at the University of Pennsylvania's business school, Wharton School, suggests it also raises questions about the company's future performance.

* Credit markets: Bond prices fell yesterday after the market concluded that comments by Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer meant that an interest-rate increase may be needed to slow a surging economy.
